cards.title: This Galápagos Fish Doesn't Swim—It Walks in Lipstick
cards.body: Found on the ocean floor around the Galápagos Islands, the red-lipped batfish is an exceptionally clumsy swimmer. Instead of gliding through water, it walks across the sandy seabed using modified pectoral and pelvic fins like miniature legs. Topped with a horn-like snout that lures prey and vivid, crimson lips that resemble freshly applied lipstick, this strange bottom-dweller looks ready for a night out on the reef.

cards.title: British Coal Mines Kept Live Canaries on Duty Until 1986
cards.body: The image of a canary in a coal mine feels like a Victorian relic, but the British government did not retire its working mine canaries until December 30, 1986. Over 200 colliery birds were phased out that year in favor of electronic gas detectors called 'electronic noses.' Despite their service, the digital monitors were far more reliable and spared hundreds of birds from dangerous underground shifts.

cards.title: Horseshoe Crabs Have Sky-Blue Blood That Protects Modern Medicine
cards.body: Horseshoe crabs do not have red blood. Instead of iron-based hemoglobin, their oxygen travels via copper-based hemocyanin, giving their blood an otherworldly milky-blue color. Even stranger, their blood cells clot almost instantaneously in the presence of bacterial endotoxins. For decades, medical labs have harvested this blue fluid to create tests that ensure every human vaccine, IV drip, and surgical implant is completely free of bacterial contamination.

cards.title: The Secretary Bird Kills Cobras With a 15-Millisecond Stomp
cards.body: The African secretary bird hunts deadly venomous snakes, including cobras and adders, using martial-arts-level precision. When attacking, it stomps downward with its long, muscular legs, striking with roughly 195 Newtons of force—five times its own body weight. Even more impressive is the speed: the entire kick makes contact for a mere 15 milliseconds, about ten times faster than the blink of a human eye, leaving snakes no time to retaliate.

cards.title: Male Bowerbirds Woo Mates by Hoarding Mountains of Blue Trash
cards.body: To attract a mate, the male satin bowerbird constructs an elaborate avenue of upright twigs and decorates the surrounding courtyard with a relentless color scheme: pure blue. Males spend weeks scavenging for blue berries, flowers, parrot feathers, and human trash like bottle caps, straws, and clothespins. Female bowerbirds tour multiple bowers like art critics, choosing mates with the most impressive, neatly curated blue exhibits.

quizzes.question: How does the red-lipped batfish primarily move along the seafloor?
options: It uses modified fins to walk across the sand
It propels itself with high-pressure water jets
It rolls along the bottom like an aquatic tumbleweed
It hitches rides by latching onto sea turtles
quizzes.explanation: Red-lipped batfish are poor swimmers and instead use their pectoral and pelvic fins like legs to crawl along the ocean floor.

quizzes.question: When did British coal mines officially replace working canaries with electronic detectors?
quizzes.explanation: Canaries served as toxic gas alarms in British coal mines until December 30, 1986, when electronic detectors replaced them.

quizzes.question: What gives horseshoe crab blood its distinct milky-blue color?
options: A dietary pigment absorbed from blue-green algae
quizzes.explanation: Horseshoe crab blood relies on copper-based hemocyanin to transport oxygen, turning it bright blue when oxygenated.

quizzes.question: How do secretary birds disable venomous snakes without getting bitten?
options: They deliver a lightning-fast kick to the snake's head
They drop stones onto snakes from high altitudes
They squirt irritating stomach acid into the snake's eyes
They bury the snakes under loose dirt until they suffocate
quizzes.explanation: Secretary birds deliver a stomp with five times their own body weight in a strike that contacts the snake for only 15 milliseconds.

quizzes.question: Which color of objects do male satin bowerbirds obsessively collect to decorate their display grounds?
quizzes.explanation: Male satin bowerbirds gather blue berries, feathers, and plastic items like bottle caps and straws to entice females.

misconceptions.claim: British coal mines stopped using live canaries in the 19th century.
misconceptions.explanation: Canaries were used in British coal mines well into the late 20th century, officially retiring only on December 30, 1986.

misconceptions.claim: All animals with circulatory systems have red blood.
misconceptions.explanation: Horseshoe crabs and many mollusks have bright blue blood because they use copper-based hemocyanin instead of iron-based hemoglobin.
